entrypoints.summary: The minimized trigger creates a directory, mounts ptyfs, opens that directory, and invokes compat_30_getdents with length 0x2c.
The generated C reproducer calls __mount50, open, and SYS_compat_30_getdents (syscall 272) in a repeated multi-process runner.

affected_components.role: Generates directory entries one at a time and copies them to userland using uiomove; maintains uio_resid and emits synthetic '.'/'..' entries.

negative_controls: No observed execution result for the reproducer on a fixed kernel is supplied; only a successful syzbot patch-test status is recorded.
observability.positive_marker: ASan Unauthorized Access reports an 8-byte write to a MallocRedZone with ptyfs_readdir in the stack.

preconditions: The demonstrated sequence must be able to create a mountpoint and successfully mount ptyfs; authorization requirements are not established by this bundle.
The reported oracle used a NetBSD amd64 kernel with KASAN, KASAN_PANIC, pool quarantine, and KCOV enabled.

impact.affected_asset: Kernel memory safety and kernel availability under the instrumented configuration.
impact.attacker_capability: Trigger the documented sanitizer fault through the supplied local ptyfs mount and compatibility-getdents syscall sequence; privilege requirements for mounting ptyfs and exploitation beyond the fault are not established.
impact.security_effect: KASAN-detected out-of-bounds write and resulting NetBSD kernel panic in the tested configuration.

causal_trace.summary: A local syscall sequence mounts ptyfs, opens its root directory, and supplies a 0x2c length to compat_30_getdents.
Before the fix, the synthetic '.'/'..' loop was bounded by i < 2 but not by remaining uio_resid; the patch adds the missing requirement uio_resid >= UIO_MX.
The reported execution reaches compat_30_sys_getdents, VOP_READDIR, and ptyfs_readdir, where ASan reports an 8-byte write to a MallocRedZone.
Under the KASAN-enabled tested kernel, the unauthorized write produces a kernel panic.

failure.operation: 8-byte write detected by ASan in ptyfs_readdir while servicing compat_30_sys_getdents

primary_invariant.statement: Each synthetic directory record emitted by ptyfs_readdir must have at least UIO_MX bytes available in uio->uio_resid.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The pre-fix loop emitted up to two synthetic records based only on i < 2; the remediation shows that it lacked the uio->uio_resid >= UIO_MX condition.

quality.review_notes: Mechanism is grounded in the exact remediation diff, pinned fixed source, minimized syscall trigger, and KASAN stack. The supplied source file is post-fix, so vulnerable control flow is reconstructed from the diff. Mount authorization, deployment reachability, a post-fix run log, and exploitability beyond the observed sanitizer panic remain unestablished.

remediation.invariant_restored: The synthetic '.'/'..' emission loop proceeds only while fewer than two entries have been considered and at least UIO_MX residual bytes remain.

state_context.attacker_state_setup: The supplied trigger creates a mountpoint and calls __mount50 for ptyfs before opening the directory and issuing compat_30_getdents.
data_structure_invariants: Synthetic '.' and '..' records require UIO_MX residual bytes before emission.

numeric_domains.attacker_constraints: The fix requires it to be at least UIO_MX before each synthetic record is emitted.
numeric_domains.name: uio->uio_resid

state_context.state_machine: Mount ptyfs, open its root directory, then enumerate it through the compatibility getdents path.

oracle.expected_negative: With the residual-space guard applied, the synthetic-entry loop does not emit when uio_resid is below UIO_MX; the issue record reports the submitted patch test as OK, but no post-fix execution log is supplied.
oracle.expected_positive: On the reported vulnerable kernel and trigger, an ASan Unauthorized Access report identifies an 8-byte MallocRedZone write with ptyfs_readdir in the stack.
